title: Transformation frameworks: dbt, SQLMesh, Spark
summary: How dbt, SQLMesh and Spark structure transformations, test them and ship them safely through environments and CI.

blocks.text: 31.1 Why transformation needs a framework

A warehouse can run any `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT`. What it cannot do on its own is manage hundreds of such statements: their dependency order, environments, tests, documentation and safe deployment. Transformation frameworks add that software-engineering layer on top of SQL (and Python).

items: **Dependency graph** inferred from references between models, not maintained by hand.
**Materialisation logic**: you write a `SELECT`; the framework generates the DDL/DML for a view, table or incremental merge.
**Tests and audits** next to the code.
**Environments**: dev, CI and prod built from the same code into different schemas.
**Docs and lineage** generated from the project.

blocks.text: 31.2 dbt: models, materializations, tests

In dbt a **model** is a `SELECT` in a `.sql` file. `{{ ref('stg_orders') }}` resolves to the right relation for the current environment and records the dependency. `{{ source('shop', 'orders') }}` points to raw tables declared in YAML, which can carry freshness rules checked by `dbt source freshness`.

head: Materialization
What dbt builds
Use when
rows: Small to medium marts; simplicity first
Inserts or merges only new/changed rows
Large facts where a full rebuild is too slow or costly
Inlined as a CTE into dependants
Reusable logic that should not exist as a relation
A warehouse-managed materialized view or dynamic table, where the adapter supports it
Let the warehouse handle refresh; check adapter support

blocks.title: models/marts/fct_orders.sql (Snowflake)

blocks.text: Incremental models drift. A filter on `max(updated_at)` misses late rows older than the lookback, and a logic change only applies to new rows. Schedule periodic `--full-refresh` runs or rebuild by partition, and test row counts against the source.

blocks.title: models/marts/_marts.yml
blocks.text:
models:
  - name: fct_orders
    columns:
      - name: order_id
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: customer_id
        data_tests:
          - relationships:
              to: ref('dim_customers')
              field: customer_id
exposures:
  - name: revenue_dashboard
    type: dashboard
    owner: {name: Finance Analytics, email: finance-analytics@example.com}
    depends_on: [ref('fct_orders')]

dbt 1.8 renamed the `tests:` key to `data_tests:` (the old key still works) and added *unit tests* that check model logic on fixed input rows. **Snapshots** implement SCD Type 2 with a `timestamp` or `check` strategy (chapter 9); newer versions define them in YAML. **Exposures** declare downstream dashboards or apps so lineage reaches the consumer.
31.3 SQLMesh: model kinds, plans, virtual environments

SQLMesh shares dbt's idea (SQL models in a graph) but differs in state management. It parses SQL with SQLGlot, so it understands column-level lineage and can classify a change as *breaking* or *non-breaking*.

blocks.title: models/fct_orders.sql
blocks.text:
MODEL (
  name analytics.fct_orders,
  kind INCREMENTAL_BY_TIME_RANGE (
    time_column order_date
  ),
  cron '@daily',
  grain order_id
);

SELECT order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount
FROM analytics.stg_orders
WHERE order_date BETWEEN @start_ds AND @end_ds

items: **Intervals**: SQLMesh records which time intervals each model has processed, so `sqlmesh run` fills only missing ones and backfills are explicit.
**Plans**: `sqlmesh plan dev` diffs local code against an environment, shows affected models and the backfill needed, and applies it on confirmation.

**Virtual environments**: physical tables are versioned by a fingerprint of their logic; environments are layers of views. Promoting to prod swaps views instead of recomputing, if the same version was already built.
**Audits** are blocking checks run after a model is evaluated; *tests* are unit tests on fixture data.

blocks.text: The virtual-environment idea matters for cost: in dbt, a dev or CI build normally recomputes models into a separate schema; in SQLMesh, unchanged models are shared and a promotion can be a metadata-only operation.
31.4 Spark and PySpark for heavy transforms

SQL frameworks cover most warehouse modelling. Spark earns its place when data is large (many TB per run), logic is not naturally SQL (parsing, ML features, complex nested JSON), or the target is an open table format on object storage that several engines read (chapter 21).

blocks.title: Deduplicate CDC and overwrite partitions in an Iceberg table
blocks.text:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F, Window

w = Window.partitionBy("order_id").orderBy(F.col("updated_at").desc())
latest = (spark.table("lake.bronze.orders_cdc")
          .where(F.col("ingest_date") == "2025-03-14")
          .withColumn("rn", F.row_number().over(w))
          .where("rn = 1").drop("rn"))

latest.writeTo("lake.silver.orders").overwritePartitions()

`overwritePartitions()` replaces only the partitions present in the DataFrame, which makes the job idempotent per day. dbt and SQLMesh can also target Spark through adapters, so the choice is not exclusive.
31.5 Environments, CI/CD and slim CI

blocks.title: Slim CI
blocks.text:
# compare against production artifacts (manifest.json) and build only what changed
dbt build --select state:modified+ --defer --state ./prod-artifacts

`state:modified+` selects changed models and their descendants; `--defer` resolves refs to unchanged models against production, so CI does not rebuild the whole project. On a 1,500-model project this turns a two-hour CI run into minutes. SQLMesh reaches a similar result through plans against a PR environment. In both, add a data diff on key marts so reviewers see how numbers changed, not only that the SQL compiles.

blocks.title: Cutting CI cost on a large dbt project
blocks.text: A marketplace platform team had 900 dbt models and full rebuilds in CI costing several warehouse-hours per pull request. They introduced slim CI with deferral, moved two 5 TB event models to incremental by date with a weekly full refresh, and added unit tests for revenue logic.
items: CI time dropped from over an hour to under ten minutes for typical changes.
Incremental drift was caught by a nightly row-count reconciliation against bronze.

blocks.text: Jinja macros make dbt flexible but can turn models into unreadable code generators. Keep macros for genuinely repeated patterns and keep model SQL readable.

blocks.title: Choose a framework for a migration
blocks.text: A team runs 300 stored procedures in a warehouse, including three daily fact tables of about 2 billion rows each. They want version control, tests, cheap CI and the option to move silver to Iceberg later. Propose a framework (or combination), materialisation per layer, CI strategy and migration order.
hints: Which procedures hide side effects or ordering assumptions?
How do you prove the new models produce the same numbers?

items: Frameworks add dependency graphs, materialisations, tests, environments and docs on top of SQL.
dbt: models, `ref`/`source`, view/table/incremental/ephemeral, data and unit tests, snapshots, exposures.
SQLMesh: model kinds, interval tracking, plans, virtual environments, audits; understands SQL semantically.
Spark is for large or non-SQL transformations; `overwritePartitions` gives idempotent writes.
Slim CI (`state:modified+ --defer`) builds only what changed; add data diffs for reviewers.

blocks.q: What does --defer do in a dbt CI run?
options: Delays the run until production finishes
Resolves refs to unselected models against another environment's relations, such as production
blocks.explain: Deferral lets CI build only modified models while reading unchanged parents from production. It does not delay runs or skip tests.

blocks.q: Why can SQLMesh promote a change to production without recomputing?
options: It caches query results in the BI tool
Physical tables are versioned by fingerprint and environments are views that can be repointed
blocks.explain: If the same model version was built in a dev environment, prod views are switched to that physical table. SQLMesh does materialise tables; it just shares them across environments.

blocks.q: An incremental dbt model filters on max(updated_at) with no lookback. What is the main risk?
options: The model will always fully refresh
Late-arriving rows with older timestamps are never loaded
blocks.explain: Rows that arrive after the high-water mark but carry an older timestamp fall below the filter. A lookback window, merge on key and periodic full refresh mitigate it.

blocks.q: When is Spark the stronger choice than dbt on a warehouse?
options: For multi-TB deduplication of nested CDC data written to an open table format
For a 50-row seed of country codes
blocks.explain: Spark fits large, non-SQL-friendly workloads and open-format targets. Small seeds and staging views are simpler in a SQL framework.
